custom_logic_notes: Fibonacci retracement EA placing two pending limit orders at user-defined 50% and 61% Fib levels. Direction is user-selected (bull/bear). Spread is incorporated into SL calculation (3*spread buffer). Partial close logic triggers when price exceeds dTarget2: closes half of each position and moves SL to entry price (breakeven stop). The dLotSize function computes volume based on account balance, risk percentage, pip distance to SL, and tick value/tick size ratio. Entry orders are only placed once (guarded by bTrade1/bTrade2 flags). Partial close also only fires once per trade (guarded by bTrade1PartiallyClosed/bTrade2PartiallyClosed). Position identification for partial close uses symbol match AND open price match against the Fib levels, which is fragile if orders are partially filled at different prices.
python_conversion_notes: 1) Fibonacci levels are user-input prices (not computed from swing high/low), so Python version needs equivalent parameterization. 2) Spread-dependent SL calculation means tick data is important for accurate backtesting. 3) Partial close + modify (breakeven) logic requires careful order state tracking. 4) Position matching by open price is fragile — recommend matching by comment/tag instead. 5) The 0.7% / (dRisk-0.7)% risk split is hardcoded and should be parameterized. 6) Lot digit detection logic is broker-specific; Python version should handle this via API lot step size. 7) Only Trade.mqh is used (standard MT5 library), so no custom indicator dependencies to port. 8) Pending limit orders require proper order lifecycle management in Python (placement, fill detection, partial close, modification).
